issues.description: Normalization contract covers ClassName only; other escapable selector types silently violate the same invariant
issues.detail: The abstract data type here is `normalizeSelector`: given two selectors that denote the same CSS, return values that compare equal. `normalizeNodeEscaping` only handles `parser.isClassName(node)`, but IDs (`#u-m\+` vs `#u-m\00002b`), attribute values, type/tag selectors, and pseudo-class arguments are equally subject to CSS escape equivalence. A caller writing `.foo` and `.foo` will now be normalized correctly, but a caller writing `#foo\+ {} #foo\00002b {}` will still slip through. The contract of the function is 'normalize escaping across selector nodes'; the implementation honors that contract for one subtype only. Either narrow the spec (rename to `normalizeClassNameEscaping` and document the gap) or extend the implementation to all node kinds whose value getter/setter performs the same normalization.

issues.description: SPEC-MISSING: relies on undocumented getter/setter side effect of a third-party type
issues.detail: The mechanism `node.value = node.value` depends on postcss-selector-parser's ClassName implementation choosing to re-encode on assignment. That is an implementation detail of a supertype the module does not own; it is not part of the published Node contract. If postcss-selector-parser ever changes ClassName's setter (or a future Node subtype overrides `value` without this behavior), this rule silently regresses to the pre-fix bug with no test signal beyond the two added fixtures. At minimum the JSDoc should state the precondition ('requires postcss-selector-parser ClassName.value setter to canonicalize escapes') and the postcondition ('node.value is in canonical escape form'), and the test suite should pin the assumption with a direct unit test on the helper rather than only end-to-end rule tests.

issues.description: LEAKY-ABSTRACTION: helper reaches into `node.raws` past the public type
issues.detail: The `@ts-expect-error` on `node.raws?.value` is an admission that the abstraction is leaking: the helper is reading a private field of the Node type to optimize a hot path. This is acceptable as a local optimization but it couples `normalizeSelector` to the internal shape of postcss-selector-parser nodes. Consider isolating the raws probe behind a small typed helper (e.g. `hasRawValue(node)`) so the leak is named and locatable, and add a comment that the optimization is correctness-preserving (skipping nodes with no raws cannot change the canonical form because there is nothing to renormalize).

issues.description: Module boundary: escape normalization belongs in the same pass as whitespace/comment normalization, but the ordering invariant is implicit
issues.detail: `normalizeSelector` now performs three ordered steps: escaping, whitespace/comments, then node order. The ordering matters (escape normalization must precede order normalization if order ever compares values), but the contract is not stated. Adding a one-line invariant comment at the top of `normalizeSelector` ('post: returned node is canonical w.r.t. escaping, whitespace, comments, and ordering — in that order') makes the module's promise legible to future maintainers and to any new normalization step added later.

review.summary: The fix is sound for the reported bug and uses a clever, minimal mechanism — the `node.value = node.value` trick correctly delegates canonicalization to postcss-selector-parser's ClassName setter. From an ADT perspective, however, the contract is under-specified and asymmetric across subtypes: the helper normalizes ClassName escaping only, while ID, attribute, tag, and pseudo selectors are equally subject to CSS escape equivalence and will continue to produce false negatives in `no-duplicate-selectors`. The implementation also depends on an undocumented getter/setter behavior of a third-party type and reaches into `node.raws` past the public interface, so the abstraction is mildly leaky and the spec is missing. Recommend stating the pre/postconditions explicitly, pinning the third-party assumption with a direct unit test, and either extending the helper to the other escapable node kinds or narrowing the function's name and docstring to match what it actually promises. Decision label: SPEC-MISSING with a partial LSP-VIOLATION across selector-node subtypes.
